bullets.title: MRVL: AI ASIC momentum drives ~10% premarket surge; NVDA CEO calls it 'next $1T company'
bullets.body: Marvell surged ~10% premarket (up 91% since May 11 and 230% in 2 months, now ~$275B cap) after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called MRVL the 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex; photonics basket +11.7% in sympathy. News also that Marvell will design a networking chip for Google to be manufactured on Intel's 18A process, with mass production by end-2027. Debate now centers on correct multiple for FY28 EPS vs. NVDA/AVGO.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $84.75B equity raise priced; Gemini at 900M+ MAU, 2027 capex to 'significantly increase'
bullets.body: Alphabet priced an upsized $84.75B capital raise (from $80B) including 25.5M secondary shares at $355.20, $15B convertible, $10B private placement (Berkshire $10B at ~$350), and a $40B ATM starting Q3 2026—all to fund AI infrastructure. Separately, Google disclosed Gemini App at 900M+ MAU as of May, raised 2026 capex guidance to $180-190B, and guided 2027 capex to 'significantly increase,' citing 'unprecedented internal and external demand for AI compute resources.'

bullets.title: AVGO: FY27 AI revenue $150-200B per management; post-earnings AMA Friday
bullets.body: Per Morgan Stanley's TMT note, Broadcom's Q2 call framed FY27 AI revenue at $150-200B (~$105B ASIC + $45B networking) with FY28 AI growth ~40% y/y. JPMorgan's Harlan Sur hosting post-earnings AMA on AVGO Friday 10am ET; Wolfe also hosting post-earnings webcast at 8:30am ET June 4. Stock was +2-3% premarket.

bullets.title: NVDA: DA Davidson adds to Best-of-Breed Bison list; Computex takeaways bullish on TCO leadership
bullets.body: DA Davidson added NVDA to its triannual Best-of-Breed Bison list of highest-quality stocks with a 5-year investment horizon. Citi's Computex takeaways describe NVDA cementing AI chip leadership; Morgan Stanley notes Vera Rubin reinforces ~85% accelerator share with CPU revenue at $20B. Oracle publicly backed Vera orders at Computex.

bullets.title: EQIX: Citi adds to Focus List; bullish on AI inference/agentic workload tailwind
bullets.body: Citi added Equinix to its Focus List following REITweek meetings, citing the company's positioning as a net beneficiary of expanding AI inference and agentic workloads driving interconnection demand. Citi believes EQIX can reach the high end of FY26 ARR growth (+9-10%), with PT $1,240 implying >15% upside. Stock was ~2% higher on the news; DLR maintained Buy on similar 2026 growth catalysts.

bullets.title: META: Morgan Stanley reiterates Top Pick; four AI monetization paths worth $4-12+ EPS
bullets.body: MS reiterates META as Top Pick, identifying four AI revenue opportunities of $1-3 EPS each: AI search/commerce ($10-30B opportunity), creator/consumer subscriptions ($7B/$2 EPS), core ad upside (+1% = $3.5B revenue/$1 EPS), and neocloud monetization. Stock was +4% in recent session, trading at 19x '26 EPS (-23% vs. TTM avg), which MS views as attractive.

bullets.title: MSFT: Truist Buy post-Build 2026; 7 proprietary AI models, Copilot super app, enterprise agent platform
bullets.body: Truist initiates MSFT Buy post-Build 2026 highlights: 7 new internally developed MAI models (including first reasoning model MAI-Thinking-1), Copilot super app unifying Chat/Cowork/Code, always-on enterprise Autopilots (Scout announced first), and Project Solara extending agents into the physical world. Citi separately noted new agentic tools and BCG data showing 75% white-collar AI adoption saving ~8hrs/week.

bullets.title: PANW: Stock -3% post-earnings despite solid beat; market punishing deceleration
bullets.body: Palo Alto beat FQ3 but stock faded -3% AH as growth decelerated to +14% y/y. NGS ARR +60% YoY, RPO +36% YoY, total revs +31% YoY; organic NNARR $20M ahead of expectations with Y/Y growth accelerating to +18% vs. +11% last quarter. SASE ARR ~$1.6B (+40% YoY), XSIAM ARR >$600M (+100% YoY). DA Davidson raised PT to $345. GS and Citi note pattern: market consistently punishes deceleration in security/data infra names regardless of absolute level.

bullets.title: ANET: BofA conference; AI/campus fastest growing, deferred revenue at ATH, GM 62-64%
bullets.body: Arista at BofA Global Technology Conference highlighted AI and campus as fastest-growing segments, with AI networking market share moving from zero to medium-high among top cloud providers. Deferred revenue at all-time high but expected to flatten as AI use cases mature. Gross margin guidance maintained at 62-64% despite supply chain cost pressures. Supply constraints in memory and silicon projected to persist for two years industry-wide.

bullets.title: ORCL: Mizuho sees FQ4 (June 10) as major catalyst; IaaS beat expected, FCF inflection to $36B by FY30
bullets.body: Mizuho previews ORCL FQ4 with consensus at $19.1B revenue/$1.97 EPS; they expect a beat driven by IaaS at $5.7B (+90% y/y). Abilene data center ramp on schedule, multi-cloud accelerating. FCF inflection expected FY29 at $4B scaling to $36B in FY30 with self-funded capex; Mizuho is materially ahead of consensus on margins/FCF. FY27 initial capex guidance disclosure is the key debate item.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS Buy $320 PT; AlphaSense investment highlights AI incumbency and accelerating M&A pace
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on Accenture with $320 PT (~19.5x FY28E EPS) after the company joined AlphaSense's $350M round (valuing it at $7.5B from $4B in 2024). AlphaSense disclosed $600M+ ARR in Q1 2026 with ~20% growth; partnership embeds market intelligence into Accenture's enterprise AI solutions. Accenture raised 2026 M&A guidance to $5B from $3B, pacing ~16 deals YTD vs. 14 in all of 2025.

bullets.title: MU: New all-time highs; MS Bull Case PT $1,650 on structural 2-3yr memory shortage
bullets.body: Micron hit a new all-time high in premarket (up 966% YTD per 52-week high data). Morgan Stanley raised Bull Case PT to $1,650 citing structural memory tightness over 2-3+ years with hyperscalers using LTAs and prepayments creating a two-tier market; MU expects $50B in buybacks FY27-28. 'Chipflation' narrative: AI infrastructure absorbing 6x rising HBM/DRAM/SSD/HDD supply.

bullets.title: TSLA: Wedbush assigns 80%+ probability to Tesla-SpaceX merger by 2027 post-SpaceX IPO
bullets.body: Wedbush maintains its view of an 80%+ chance that Tesla and SpaceX merge following SpaceX's planned IPO, citing growing operational ties between the two companies including the joint Terafab initiative. SpaceX separately announced plans to raise $75B at $135/share for a $1.75T valuation with roadshow beginning Thursday. Tesla UK sales rose 18% YoY to 2,812 units in May.

bullets.title: SHOP: $3B buyback boost fails to hold; stock -2.4% in Canadian session
bullets.body: Shopify announced a $3B increase to its share repurchase program but the stock declined 2.4% in the Canadian mid-morning session amid a broader S&P/TSX selloff (-0.32%). CLS also traded lower -2.6%.

bullets.title: CSCO: Citi Buy $112 PT; optics multi-$B business, CPO in 2027, AI data center TAM $30B by 2030
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Cisco after Cisco Live; CSCO has shipped 450K+ 400G and 40K+ 800G pluggables with laser supply chain as key constraint (investing ahead). AI optical data center TAM sized at $30B by 2030, CPO adoption expected in 2027 for AI scale-up training, coherent lite in 2028. Cloud Control platform has 50+ ecosystem partners.

bullets.title: ADBE: Bloomberg reports Wadhwani and Chakravarthy as frontrunners for next CEO
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported that David Wadhwani (Digital Media) and Anil Chakravarthy (Digital Experience) are the favorites to become Adobe's next CEO. Both lead the company's two primary business groups.

bullets.title: APP: Jefferies expert call on AppLovin e-commerce ROAS vs. Meta/Google
bullets.body: Jefferies hosted an expert call with REEKON Tools' Director of Growth, who previously managed $20-30M in paid media across Meta, Google, and AppLovin, to discuss AppLovin's return on ad spend in e-commerce and 2026 spending outlook including new Gen AI creative tools.

bullets.title: T: Oppenheimer downgrades to Perform on satellite competition risk to broadband/mobile
bullets.body: Oppenheimer downgraded AT&T to Perform from Outperform, citing increasing long-term risks to broadband and mobile subscriber growth from satellite operators.

bullets.title: WULF/IREN: MS raises WULF PT to $66.50; IREN announces 800MW Australia data center
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley hikes WULF price target to $66.50 from $42 on Muskie and Risel/McLennan site additions; also raises CIFR PT to $53.50 from $42.50 as a key ERCOT Batch Zero beneficiary (preliminary 35 GW baseload + 65 GW to be studied). IREN announced its first Australian data center—an 800MW campus in Bundey, South Australia with 330kV feeder exits and energization from 2028.

bullets.title: TMUS: Unusual options volume 240% above 30-day avg; stock -4.0%
bullets.body: T-Mobile showed unusual options activity at 240% above its 30-day average (18,265 contracts vs. 7,598 avg) while the stock was down 4.0%, per StreetAccount options alert. GFS was the highest at 348% above avg (+2.4% stock) and TENB at 406% above avg (-1.0%) ahead of William Blair Growth Stock Conference on June 4.
